messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, tom.reynolds@acme.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form: downtime carveouts & response ladder

Hi Aditya / team,

Thanks for the draft order form. Legal at Acme has a couple of sticking points on the SLA and maintenance language we need resolved before we can finalize the PO: 

- Service credits: the draft caps credits at 5% of monthly invoice per incident. Legal wants an annual cap (10% of annual spend) and clearer calculation examples.
- Uptime target: they want 99.99% for our production tier; your team proposed 99.95. They asked for objective justification for the lower target.
- Response times: for P1 incidents they want an initial response (ack + triage start) within 15 minutes and a live update cadence every 30 minutes until mitigation.
- Maintenance windows: they want a guarantee of no maintenance in our US-East peak window (Mon-Fri 09:00–17:00 ET) unless we explicitly approve; exceptions for emergency security fixes only.

We appreciate any flexibility, but also need to keep this contract feasible operationally. Can you confirm what we can accommodate and circulate a proposed redline? Attaching Acme's preferred redline to illustrate their ask.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_sla_redlines_v1.docx (attachment stub)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form: downtime carveouts & response ladder

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping legal (Lauren), Ops (Kimberly) and Platform (Marcus) to assess:

Quick summary of what I think we can do without impacting reliability or opening a bad precedent:
- Service credits: we can agree to an annual cap (10% of annual spend) instead of per-incident caps if we add a clause tying credits to cumulative annual downtime and exclude scheduled maintenance within agreed blackout windows.
- Uptime: we need to keep 99.95% for the Dedicated tier unless they opt into a higher-cost SLA (we can offer 99.99% as a paid add-on with dedicated redundancy). I'll ask Marcus to provide a short justification note (latency/redundancy/cost delta).
- Response times: 15-minute acknowledgement for P1 is aggressive; our current SLA is 30 minutes to acknowledge and 60 minutes to provide a mitigation plan. We can offer 15/30 as a premium support option.
- Maintenance windows: we can commit to no planned maintenance in their stated peak window; need to define "emergency" in text to avoid ambiguity.

I'll collect concrete redline language from Lauren and a cost delta from Marcus and share an internal consolidated redline by EOD. If that looks OK, Monica can schedule a short call with Acme this week to finalize.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Team — drafting suggested redline language below (high level):

1) Scheduled Maintenance and Blackouts
We propose adding a defined "Scheduled Maintenance" section:
- "Scheduled Maintenance" means planned changes that may require service interruptions; Redwood will provide not less than 10 business days' notice for scheduled maintenance impacting customer production endpoints. Redwood will not perform scheduled maintenance during Customer's agreed blackout windows (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 ET) unless Customer provides prior written consent. Emergency maintenance (critical security or compliance fixes that cannot be deferred) may be performed with as much notice as reasonably practicable; Redwood will notify Customer within 2 hours of commencement.

2) Service Credits — annual cap and calculation
- Credits shall accrue only for unplanned downtime during the billing period and shall be calculated as: (Downtime minutes / Total minutes in billing period) * Monthly recurring charges. Annual aggregate credit cap shall be 10% of Customer's annualized MRC. Credits do not apply where downtime is caused by Customer misconfiguration, third-party provider outages, or during Scheduled Maintenance.

3) Response and Communication Ladder
- P1: initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes (business hours), mitigation plan within 2 hours, live updates every 60 minutes.
- Offer premium support addendum for 15 minute ack / 30 minute mitig plan and 30-minute updates.

Notes/questions for Sales/Ops:
- Does Ops accept 10 business days for maintenance notice?
- Can Finance handle annual cap calculation examples for transparency?

I will produce a redline doc using the Order Form template and attach.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RF_orderform_sla_redline_track.docx (attachment stub)

Quick ops perspective — constraints and a suggested compromise: 

- 99.99% vs 99.95%: to get to 99.99% for production we'd need active cross-region redundancy and reserved replication capacity for failover; that is a ~25–35% uplift in costs (in the Dedicated scenario). We can offer 99.99% as a configurable upgrade (line-item in order form).

- Maintenance notice: 10 business days is fine for most planned maintenance. We request that the blackout be defined as a recurrent weekly window (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 ET) and that Customer allow up to two scheduled maintenance events per quarter outside that window with 48 hours notice for non-critical ops work (helps us reduce risk during major infra upgrades).

- Credits math: Ops requests an explicit exclusion for third-party cloud provider interruptions and for Customer-caused incidents. Also recommend we include a small-batch examples table — attached uptime-metrics-table.xlsx — to make the formula concrete.

If Sales wants to keep 15-minute ack as a selling point, we can draft a Premium Support addendum with guaranteed pager coverage and a separate fee.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: uptime-metrics-table.xlsx (attachment stub)

Aditya / Lauren / Kim —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and for proposing a premium support path. A few follow-ups from Acme Legal and Infra: 
- Annual cap at 10% is acceptable if you add one example calculation (we want to see how it would hit for our current MRC).
- The blackout window proposal with allowance for two out-of-window events per quarter is acceptable only if those events are scheduled with a minimum 48-hour notice and cannot be classified as "non-critical ops work" unless tied to a measurable upgrade plan.
- Regarding 99.99% as a paid add-on — can you provide the delta in price and the technical runbook for cross-region failover? Acme's infra team will need to review the runbook before agreeing to the add-on.

We are hopeful we can get to redlines this week. Monica — can we set a 30-minute call Wednesday to go over the updated doc and examples?

Best,
Samantha

1) Internal redline: Lauren will circulate an Order Form redline (RF_orderform_sla_redline_track.docx) by EOD PST today that implements:
   - Scheduled Maintenance definition with Customer blackout as requested and 48-hour exception window language.
   - Annual credit cap at 10% with sample calculation row included.
   - Response ladder kept at 30-minute P1 ack / 2-hour mitigation plan but with a Premium Support addendum drafted for 15/30/30 commitments.

2) Ops deliverable: Marcus/Kim will produce a 1-page technical note showing what is required to reach 99.99% (architecture, estimated cost uplift, and a high-level failover runbook). Target: WED COB.

3) Customer alignment: Monica — please propose three 30-minute windows on WED for a redline walkthrough with Acme (suggest 09:30, 13:00, 15:30 ET). Include the redline and the uptime examples workbook in the invite.

4) Finance/Legal: If Acme insists on any deviation from exclusions (third-party, customer-caused), flag for leadership escalation.

I will post the consolidated redline in the shared Drive link and send the calendar invite once Monica confirms times. If Acme signs off on the annual cap/blackout compromise we should be able to move to signature early next week.

—Aditya
